title: Runtime benchmarking bundles and pin contracts for verified performance profiles
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Onboarding new model artifacts to the Redwood catalog currently results in brittle or inconsistent performance claims because our verification has grown ad-hoc: single-point latency numbers, sparse sequence-length coverage, and manual pin decisions. This causes customer surprise when runtime conditions differ (longer contexts, different tokenization, bursty traffic) and increases support load.

Goal: Define and implement a repeatable 'benchmarking bundle' and a corresponding pin contract that together become the canonical artifact used to publish a Redwood-verified performance profile. The bundle + contract must capture latency distributions, throughput targets, preferred quantization/variant, and pinning rules for semantic version changes. The output will be a machine-readable bundle (artifact) stored in the profile registry and a human-friendly artifact page in the Console.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Benchmarking bundle schema specified and agreed by runtime, infra, and applied-ML teams.
- Automated harness runs produce bundles for new model uploads with coverage across at least 3 sequence-length buckets and 2 batch sizes.
- Publishing pipeline verifies bundles and creates a profile artifact in the registry with a signed attestation.
- Pin contract rules implemented: minor patch changes allowed without republish if regression < 2% latency P95 and accuracy delta < 0.5% for canonical eval set.
- Console shows per-route recommended variants and explicit pinned version with rollback instructions.

Proposed approach:
1) Define 'benchmarking bundle' schema (JSON lines): metadata (model name, model sha, container image, hardware target), microbenchmarks (latency P50/P90/P95 P99, throughput/tps, cold vs warm starts), distribution traces (histograms or buckets), cost estimates per token, canonical eval results (dataset name/version + metric), and recommended serving variant (quantized FP16/int8).
2) Standardize three sequence-length buckets: short (<=64), medium (65-512), long (513-4096). For each bucket run: single-request latency (P50/P95/P99), 8/16/32-token streaming tokens/sec, and batching throughput for batch sizes [1,8,16].
3) Implement harness glue in onboarding pipeline to spin dedicated ephemeral clusters (runtime team) and record deterministic runs (seeded inputs), upload artifacts to registry, sign via KMS.
4) Define pin contract policy doc: pin to major.minor (e.g., v2.3) by default; patch releases (v2.3.1->v2.3.2) may be auto-accepted if automated regression checks pass. Major/minor changes require explicit republish and manual sign-off. Provide machine-check algorithm (thresholds) and a human override flow.
5) Console/registry integration: display bundle metadata, links to raw harness logs, and a one-click 'request republish' for customers or internal SRE.

Acceptance criteria for MVP: 
- Bundle schema implemented and reviewed (schema file checked into performance-catalog repo).
- Onboarding pipeline produces one verified bundle for the next model candidate during staging.
- Registry UI surfaces the pinned version and the delta between current live and pinned variant.
- Documentation (Confluence) drafted with the pin contract and steps for runtime/ops to respond to regressions.

Out of scope for MVP: automated rollback of live traffic, advanced drift-detection, full multi-region matrix benchmarking (will follow in follow-up tickets).

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Long benchmark runs tie up CI/GPU resources. Mitigation: use smaller sampling seeds for initial verification and reserve longer nightly runs for full endorsement.
- Risk: False negatives from noisy infra. Mitigation: run each microbenchmark 3x and use median; require signed-run provenance.

Stakeholders: runtime (Priya Desai), infra/ops (Ethan Cho), applied ML (Rita Kumari), console/product (Miguel Santos), security/KMS (Jorge Alvarez).
comments: 2025-03-02 - Asha Patel: Initial write-up and RFC posted. Asked runtime and applied-ML to review the proposed bucket boundaries; flagged resource implications for infra.
2025-03-03 - Priya Desai (runtime): Agree with bucket choices but asked to add a 'cold start' contended CPU test and include KV cache warm/warmest states. Added to schema proposal.

2025-03-04 - Rita Kumari (applied-ML): Requested canonical eval set list and exact metric definitions; suggested adding an 'end-to-end quality' metric (ROUGE/EM) for generation models to guard against quantization regressions.

2025-03-05 - Miguel Santos (product): Reviewed acceptance criteria and requested the pin contract include an explicit 'customer notification' step for any auto-accepted patch that affects latency >1% for customers on Dedicated.
